vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.9

The cellcog skill acts as a bridge to an external AI service (cellcog.ai), requiring the agent to transmit local file contents via <SHOW_FILE> tags. Most significantly, the SKILL.md instructions direct the agent to execute a command to modify the OpenClaw gateway configuration (gateway.tools.allow) to enable high-privilege session management tools (sessions_send and sessions_list). While these capabilities are documented as necessary for the tool's 'notify' mode and background daemon functionality, the request to programmatically lower the security boundaries of the host platform and the inherent data exposure to a third-party service constitute high-risk behaviors.

llm.summary: The skill asks for your CellCog API key and instructs the agent to read arbitrary absolute file paths and optionally pass an OpenClaw session key to an external service — this can lead to unintended upload/exfiltration of sensitive local data and those sensitive session tokens are not declared as required inputs.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (any-input→any-output) reasonably explains needing an SDK (python3) and a CellCog API key; however the runtime instructions require the agent to supply absolute local file paths that the service will read and process, and to optionally forward an OpenClaw 'notify_session_key' — these data-access needs are not declared in the skill metadata (no required config paths or additional env vars), creating a gap between stated requirements and actual data access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs using <SHOW_FILE>/absolute/path</SHOW_FILE> tags so CellCog will read arbitrary files from the host and process them, and it suggests passing an OpenClaw session key (notify_session_key) to the remote service for notifications. Those instructions allow transmission of any local files and session tokens to cellcog.ai without any in-file restrictions or warnings — broad file/system access that can easily exfiltrate secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the instructions recommend 'pip install cellcog' if import fails. Relying on pip at runtime is common but unpinned; because this is instruction-only, the installer can cause arbitrary code to be downloaded/executed during install. The lack of a pinned package/version or provenance note increases supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The declared required env var is only CELLCOG_API_KEY, which matches the service. However the instructions instruct users to provide a notify_session_key (an OpenClaw session token) as an argument — a sensitive credential that is not declared in requires.env. The skill does not warn that file contents or session keys will be transmitted to an external service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only, has no install spec or code files, does not request always:true, and does not appear to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It does not ask for persistent agent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will upload any absolute local file paths you put in <SHOW_FILE> tags and may accept an OpenClaw session key to send notifications — that can expose sensitive files or session tokens to cellcog.ai. Before installing or using: (1) don't include or upload secrets or system files (password stores, SSH keys, /etc, etc.); (2) avoid passing session tokens (notify_session_key) unless you fully trust and have reviewed the service's handling of tokens; (3) create and use an API key with minimal scope and rotate it after testing; (4) verify the 'cellcog' pip package provenance and consider installing in an isolated environment; (5) if you need to test, do so in a sandboxed agent or VM with only non-sensitive data. If the ability to selectively limit which files are read or to avoid sending session identifiers is important, ask the maintainer for explicit privacy/data-handling documentation and for the skill to declare any required tokens/paths in metadata.
